rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Six of the Ten reciters read malik without alif: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Abu Ja‘far.
rows.anchor: Aşere’den جع,ف,ك,ح,د,ا yani Nâfi‘, İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, İbn Âmir, Hamza, Ebû Ca‘fer kıraatlerinde elifsiz olarak مَلِكِ يَوْمِ الدّين okunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim, Kisai, Ya‘qub, and Khalaf al-‘Ashir read mālik with alif; Elmalılı says this is his own reading.
rows.anchor: ن, خل,يع,ر yani Âsım, Kisâî, Ya‘kūb, Halef-i Âşir [92] kıraatlerinde de مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدّين okunur ki bizim kıraatimiz de budur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings derive from different forms: malik from mulk as an intensive adjective, and mālik from milk as an active participle.
rows.anchor: Evvelki, mîm’in zammıyla “mülk” masdarından sıfat-ı müşebbehe sîgası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both words concern power: malik directly governs human persons, while mālik directly controls material property and its benefits.
rows.anchor: Biri evvelen ve bizzat nüfûs-i insâniye üzerinde tasarruf, diğeri de evvelen ve bizzat emvâlin a‘yân ve menâfi‘i üzerinde tasarruf kuvvetidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Melikiyyat is public authority over rational people for common benefit, exercised through deliberation, commands, prohibitions, promises, warnings, and social order.
rows.anchor: “Melikiyet” nef‘-i ‘âm için re’y ü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mālikiyyat is an individual's independent right and authority to control assets for private benefit.
rows.anchor: “Mâlikiyet” ise, mal olan a‘yân ve hisse-i a‘yân üzerinde ferdin nef‘-i hâssı için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Private life and benefit depend on individual ownership, while common welfare depends on public dominion through social order, the state, and its head.
rows.anchor: Bir memlekette hayat ve menfa‘at-i hâssa milk ve mâlik ile, yani milkiyyet-i ferdiye ile kāimdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Private and public authority sustain one another; stability requires recognizing their dependence and a just balance between them.
rows.anchor: Bunların kıvâmı da her ikisinin zâtî ve asîlî olmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute collectivism that crushes individuals and private ownership leaves society like a body whose senses are paralyzed.
rows.anchor: Ferdi ve milkiyyet-i ferdiyeyi boğan ictimâ‘iyyet-i mutlaka, a‘zâsının bütün havâssı felce uğrayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute individualism that destroys society and shared ownership resembles a dying body's final convulsion.
rows.anchor: Cemiyeti, mülkiyyet-i ictimâ‘iyeyi boğan ferdiyyet-i mutlaka da uzviyeti münhâl olup canı boğazına gelmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loss of either private ownership or public dominion is disastrous, usually bringing the loss of the other as well.
rows.anchor: Bunun için milk ve mülkten her birinin zayâ‘ı bir felâkettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute ownership and sovereignty properly belong to the Lord of the Worlds alone.
rows.anchor: Gerek mâlikiyyet-i mutlaka ve gerek melikiyyet-i mutlaka ikisi de bi’l-asâle Rabbü’l-âlemîn’e mahsustur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human claims to ownership and rule are only relative, delegated, and borrowed because people do not control their own lives.
rows.anchor: hayâtı kendi yedinde olmayan beşerin bu sıfatlarla ittisâfı bi’t-tab‘izâfî, niyâbî ve müste‘âr olduğu âşikârdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse announces that this derivative share will be taken away in the future, especially the Hereafter, leaving God's eternal and real dominion.
rows.anchor: istikbalde ‘ale’l-husûs âhirette bunun dahi meslûb olacağını ve o zaman yalnız Cenâb-ı Rabbü’l-âlemîn’in ezelî ve ebedî olan mâlikiyyet-i hakīkiye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses depict that day as belonging to God alone, when no soul controls anything for another and all affairs are God's.
rows.anchor: İlk nazarda bu inzar ne kadar müdhiştir! “Benim benim” derken, memleket

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning's practical benefit is to feel the loss beforehand; it is not despairing, since the true Owner gathers all existence into His merciful power rather than letting it vanish into nothing.
rows.anchor: âyet-i celîle ye’s-âver değildir. İzâfî ve niyâbî olan mâlikiyet veya melikiyetin zâil olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those belonging to God's realm will receive happiness according to their rank, while those outside it face lasting deprivation and cannot change allegiance then.
rows.anchor: memleket-i rabbâniyenin tâbi‘iyetini taşıyanlar o gün hisse-i sa‘âdetlerini mertebelerine göre bâliğan mâ-belağ alacaklar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mālik reading conveys warning and good news from the angle of private ownership, while malik conveys them from the angle of public sovereignty.
rows.anchor: “mâlik” kıraati bu inzâr u tebşîri milkiyyet-i ferdiye nokta-i nazarından, “melik” kıraati de mülkiyyet-i ictimâ‘iye nokta-i nazarından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine mercy distributes the two warnings across the readings; their separation, rather than combining them in one reading, displays the greatest eloquence.
rows.anchor: İki inzârın bir kıraatte cem‘ine Fâtiha’da rahmâniyyet-i ilâhiye müsaade etmemiş ve en büyük belâgat bunların iki kıraate tevzî‘inde tecellî etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first three verses form one proposition, that praise belongs to God, supported by five proofs drawn from His essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha’da ilk vakf-ı tâmmın mutazammın olduğu bu üç âyet bir matlub ile beş delîlinden mürekkeb bir kaziyyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves praise essentially because He is God, and through the attributes of Lord of the Worlds, Merciful, Compassionate, and Master of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: Sıfaten müstahiktir, çünkü Rabbü’l-âlemîn’dir ve çünkü Rahmân’dır ve çünkü Rahîm’dir ve çünkü Mâlik-i yevm-i dîn’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first proof is self-evident; the remaining proofs summarize arguments from the ordered cosmos about origin and return, which the Qur'an will detail.
rows.anchor: Diğerleri de enfüs ü âfâkın mülâhazasıyla nizâm-ı âlemden müstenbat mebde’ ü me‘âd delillerinin icmâlidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report of God's attributes also implies a command: whoever honors perfection, beneficence, future hope, or fear should praise the God who encompasses them all.
rows.anchor: Ey insanlar, ey zevi’l-‘ukūl! Siz hüsn-i mahza, kemâl-i mutlaka ta‘zîm edenlerden iseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing these grounds, rational hearers naturally ask how and in what manner they should praise God, setting up the next verse.
rows.anchor: Acaba Allah teâlâ’ya nasıl ve ne suretle hamd edelim?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the verse as worshipping and serving God alone and seeking aid and care from Him alone.
rows.anchor: Meâl: Sâde sana ederiz kulluğu, ibadeti ve sâde senden dileriz ʿavni, inâyeti yâ Rab!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative meaning 'say this' is implicit; placing the independent pronoun before the verb expresses exclusivity: to You alone, not another.
rows.anchor: gelmesi kasr ve ihtisas ifade ettiğinden “başkasına değil ancak sana” demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal usage, worship is a special act of obedience that earns reward, depends on intention, and expresses nearness to God.
rows.anchor: “ibadet”, niyete mütevakkıf olarak yapılmasında sevab olan ve Cenâb-ı Allah’a kurbet ifade eden tâ‘at-i mahsûsadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taat is an act rewarded whether or not it depends on intention or the doer knows for whom it is done.
rows.anchor: “Tâat”, niyete mütevakkıf olsun olmasın ve kimin için yapıldığı bilinsin bilinmesin yapılması sevab olan fiili yapmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbat is a rewarded act performed with awareness of the person one seeks to approach, even when intention is not required.
rows.anchor: “Kurbet”, niyete mütevakkıf olmasa bile yapılması sevab olan fiili kime yapıldığını bilerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every worship act is both qurbat and taat, and every qurbat is taat, but the reverse implications do not hold.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh her ibadet Allah’a bir kurbet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection to know God is taat but not qurbat while its intended object remains unknown, and without intention it is not worship.
rows.anchor: Meselâ ma‘rifetullah için fikr ü nazar bir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an recitation, charity, aid, endowment, and freeing slaves without required intention are qurbat and taat but not ibadat; prayer, fasting, alms, pilgrimage, and jihad with intention are all three.
rows.anchor: Kur’an okumak, muhtaçlara yardım etmek, sadaka vermek, vakıf yapmak, köle azat etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal worship is conscious obedience and nearness directed only to God through the person's whole spiritual and bodily, outward and inward existence.
rows.anchor: Demek ki ibâdet-i şer‘iye, insanın rûhen ve cismen, zâhiren ve bâtınen bütün mevcûdiyetiyle yalnız Allah’a yapılan şuurlu bir tâat ve kurbettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intention is a present, created will to obey God and draw near through the act; resolve comes before action, purpose accompanies it, and intention joins knowledge to the act.
rows.anchor: Niyet ise yapılacak fiilin îcâdında ancak Allah’a tâat ve tekarrub kast etmek demek olan irâde-i hâdisedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Full awareness, containing both knowledge and will, belongs to the soul and heart.
rows.anchor: Hem ilim ve hem iradeyi ihtivâ eden bu şu‘ûr-i tâm rûh ve kalbin bir işidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship also requires an outwardly manifested act of obedience; inward reflection alone may be taat and qurbat but does not become worship.
rows.anchor: ind-i ilâhîde tâat olan bir fiil izhâr edilmiş olmak lâzımdır ki ibadet olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith requires at least verbal confession as well as inward assent, while an unexpressed inner thought is insufficient as worship.
rows.anchor: imanda sadece tasdîk-i kalbî kifayet etmez de bunun hiç olmazsa lisânen ikrar ile zâhire ihrâc edilmesi dahi lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: External ritual acts without intention are not worship: sleep is not prayer, hunger is not fasting, giving is not alms, travel is not pilgrimage, and fighting is not jihad.
rows.anchor: Niyetsiz yatıp kalkmak namaz değil, niyetsiz aç durmak oruç değil, niyetsiz sadaka vermek, i‘âne yapmak zekât değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bad intention, meaning an aim other than obedience and nearness to God, prevents an act from counting as worship.
rows.anchor: sû’-i niyetle, yani Allah’a itaat ve kurbet kasdından mâ‘adâ bir maksadla yapılan fiiller hiç ibadet olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turkish tapmak and tapınmak suggest indiscriminate or unconscious obedience and are associated with idols and the cross, so translating worship that way debases the language; kulluk is more aware but weaker than worship.
rows.anchor: “tapmak” ve “tapınmak” kelimelerinde az çok ne yaptığını bilmemek gibi bir şuursuzluk mânası anlarız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before later legal convention, the shared lexical root meaning of worship should be considered; its broadest sense appears in ubudet or abed and includes worshipper and object of worship.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna (ع ب د) madde-i asliyesinin en umûmî olan mânası ne ise odur ki bu da “ubûdet” veya “abed” masdarlarındandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubudet is the broadest term, while ibadat is narrower; ubudiyet displays humility and ibadat expresses its strongest form, including awe and reverence.
rows.anchor: “ubûdet” lisân-ı Arab’da tezellül mânasını mutazammındır. “Ubûdiyet” izhâr-ı tezellül, “ibadet” bunun daha kuvvetlisi

rows.speaker: cumhûr-i müfessirîn
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes define worship as the utmost degree of humility, which entails complete obedience without asking the reason.
rows.anchor: cumhûr-i müfessirîn bunu “gāye-i hudû‘un aksâsı” diye tefsir ederler

rows.speaker: İbn Sikkît
rows.claim: Ibn Sikkit is reported in Abu Hayyan's tafsir as deriving ibadat from the sense of tajrid, or detachment.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Ebû Hayyân’da İbn Sikkît’ten ibâdetin tecrid mânasından me’huz olduğu da nakledilmiştir

rows.speaker: Şârih-i Kāmûs
rows.claim: The commentator on the Qamus says ibadat derives from the root abed, associated with greed or anger.
rows.anchor: Şârih-i Kāmûs’un beyânına göre de ibadet, hırs veya gazab mânalarına gelen “abed” maddesinden me’huzdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says worship is doing what God approves while ubudiyet is being content with what God does; its usage can be narrower or broader, and Prophetic ubudiyet is more specific than ibadat.
rows.anchor: “İbadet”, Allah’ın râzı olduğu şeyi yapmak, “ubudiyet” de Allah’ın yaptığına râzı olmak diye de tefsir edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life travels between pleasure and pain: fear and hope repeatedly shape action, while despair extinguishes activity and absence of fear leads to transgression and waste.
rows.anchor: Kesb-i beşerin nâzımı da işte hâlden istikbâle bu korku ile ümidin mütevâlî tekabül ve tesâdümüdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope needs some fear and fear some hope for a sense of duty; the hungry work to become full and the full work from fear of hunger.
rows.anchor: Ümidin içinde bir korku, korkunun içinde bir ümit yoksa vazife hissi atâlete düşer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life is an exchange between inner and outer conditions, many of whose causes lie outside us or were not chosen by us; this makes each person sense their own incapacity.
rows.anchor: Hayât-ı beşer dâhil ile hâricin bir muâmelesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even intelligent people cannot escape dependence on hope and fear, and no individual can leave this field of helplessness alone.
rows.anchor: Fakat ne olursa olsun hiçbir ferd kendi kendine bu acz sahasından çıkamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human hope and fear have no ultimate limit; alongside particular hopes and fears, the soul is affected by boundless possibilities that converge in one ultimate source.
rows.anchor: rûh-i beşerde ne ümidin nihâyeti vardır ne de korkunun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul's attachment to an ultimate source of hope and fear is the origin of the innate ideas of worship and the object of worship, and moral character and future fortune depend on its seriousness.
rows.anchor: İşte rûh-i insânînin böyle külliyetiyle müteessir olduğu mutlak bir havf u recâ âmiline karşı duyduğu bu alâka fıtrattaki mâbud ve ibadet fikrinin menşe’idir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may become wholly captive to one limited pleasure or fear, treating its finite cause as the goal of all love or the limit of all fear and humbling themselves before it.
rows.anchor: Artık o bu ümidin âmilini öyle sevmiş veya o korkunun âmilinden öyle yılmıştır ki bunlar ona bütün sevgilerin gayesi veya bütün korkuların müntehâsı gibi görünür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such attachment to a created finite cause is the source of shirk and the many false idols, whether animate or inanimate.
rows.anchor: İnsanlara ma‘bûd-ı hakīkī ve ‘ubûdiyyet-i hakīkiye alâkasını unutturarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even those who claim no concern with worship continually replace one object of worship with another and live in uncertainty without considering death.
rows.anchor: kendilerini mâbud ve ibadet fikriyle hiç alâkadar değil gibi zannedenler her lahza böyle bir mâbud değiştirirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any heart tied wholly to mortal things is at risk of ruin because that attachment will eventually break; only the Ever-Living Sustainer can guarantee what creatures cannot.
rows.anchor: Bütün mevcûdiyetini fânîlere bağlayan her gönül

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship belongs to God alone; worshippers who serve Him are not wholly captured by other hopes and fears and can remain steady in their duties.
rows.anchor: Ve fi’l-hakīka ibadet O’nun hakkıdır ve ancak O’na ibadet edenlerdir ki diğer ümitlere, korkulara kendini tamamen kaptırmaz

rows.speaker: Aleyhi’s-salâtü ve’s-selâm Efendimiz
rows.claim: The Prophet compares a believer to fresh grain that bends in wind and rises again, but a disbeliever to a pine that breaks once and never rises.
rows.anchor: Aleyhi’s-salâtü ve’s-selâm Efendimiz buyurmuştur ki “Mü’min taze ekin gibidir, rüzgâr estikçe yatar, fakat yine doğrulur kalkar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer is attached to the Everlasting Living God, while the disbeliever is attached to what perishes.
rows.anchor: Çünkü kâfir fâniye, mü’min ise Hayy-i Bâkī’ye merbuttur

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ömeru’l-Fârûk
rows.claim: After the Prophet's death, Umar was so shaken that he denied the Prophet had died and threatened anyone who said otherwise.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömeru’l-Fârûk bile “Peygamber vefat etmedi ve etmez, her kim öyle derse vururum” demeye kadar varmıştı

rows.speaker: Sıddîk-i A‘zam Efendimiz
rows.claim: Abu Bakr recited Qur'an 3:144 to remind the Companions that Muhammad was a messenger who had died before messengers, and to restore their composure.
rows.anchor: Sıddîk-i A‘zam Efendimiz derhâl وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ

rows.speaker: Sıddîk-i A‘zam Efendimiz
rows.claim: Abu Bakr tells them that worship of Muhammad cannot continue after his death, whereas the God who sent him is the Living One who never dies.
rows.anchor: Ey mü’minler! Eğer Muhammed’e ibadet ediyorsanız işte o vefat etti ve eğer onu gönderen Allah teâlâ’ya ibadet ediyorsanız O Hayy-i lâ-yemûttur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When mortal attachments divide the sources of hope and fear, hearts pursue separate love-idols and fear-idols through irrational humiliations and cannot find calm.
rows.anchor: bir tarafta dilber sevgi mâbudları, bir tarafta da kahraman korku mâbudları dizilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope and fear must be positive and negative effects of one source so the heart can replace one with the other and find contentment; if they come from unrelated sources, pursuit yields endless exhaustion.
rows.anchor: Ümit ve korku bir mebde’den gelen ve yine onda birleşen müsbet ve menfî birer sûret-i te’sîr olarak duyulmalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water and fire analogy shows that alternating between hope and fear from unrelated sources is futile; the one Lord is what binds self, consciousness, and the external world.
rows.anchor: Fakat bunların biri suyun, diğeri ateşin eserleri ise su ile ateş beyninde hâkim bir mebde’-i müşterek de yok ise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is obedient action born from the collision of supreme love and fear, seeking ascent from total helplessness to absolute power and seeking tranquility through ultimate humility and reverence.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı fıtrat-ı beşerde ibadet, rûhu teshir eden en yüksek mahabbet ile en yüksek mehâfetin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True worship unites outward and inward submission without pride or ostentation; arrogant people, heedless optimists, and despairing pessimists are excluded from its honor.
rows.anchor: Bunun için kibr ü riya ile birleşmez ve zâhir ü bâtına inkisâmı kabul etmez

rows.speaker: e‘âzım-ı müfessirîn
rows.claim: The great exegetes paraphrase worship as bowing and humbling oneself only to God, finding tranquility through obedience because He alone is the source of all fear and hope.
rows.anchor: Bu hakikatleri telhis için e‘âzım-ı müfessirîn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone controls fear, hope, pleasure, pain, body, soul, and the inner capacities of perception and volition; these gifts should be devoted to His command with gratitude.
rows.anchor: Rûh Senin milkin, cisim Senin milkin, bütün vücûd Senin milkin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proud objector asks whether worship's humility is degrading for a soul that wants to rise or believes it has already risen.
rows.anchor: Rûh ve vicdan tezellül değil yükselmek ister, ibadet ise ma‘nâ-yı tezellülü mutazammın olduğuna göre yükselecek olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wanting to rise admits one's own need and the value of a higher state, which worship recognizes most fully.
rows.anchor: Yükselmek istemek, yükselmek ihtiyâcını teslim etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claiming to have risen already falsely treats progress as finite and decline as impossible; ascent is limitless and the danger of falling remains, so worship is pride's remedy.
rows.anchor: merâtib-i te‘âlî nâmütenâhîdir, tehlike-i sukūt ise her zaman bâkīdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility and reverence toward God provide the highest possible elevation for the human conscience through affiliation with Him.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’ya ibadetteki tezellül ve ta‘zîm vicdân-ı beşer için mümkin olan her türlü i‘tilânın fevkinde bir ulviyet temin eden bir vesîka-i intisabdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imagined worshipper pledges freedom from all but God, obedience to His commands, moral effort, and even sacrifice of life and worlds in God's path.
rows.anchor: Âlemde ben Allah’tan başkasına hürriyetimi veremem ve ancak O’na ve O’nun emrine inkıyad ederim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such faithful affiliation is the greatest human power and nobility; the Fatiha asks the speaker to say 'we,' making the pledge communal.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh bu babda Fâtiha “ben” değil “biz” deyiniz diyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first Muslims lived this spirit and spread God's exaltation across the world, whereas those who lost it bowed to worldly power.
rows.anchor: ilk Müslümanlar bütün bu rûhun içinde idiler, bu rûhu kaybedenler de dünyaya boyun eğdiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge is a heavy burden, but the dignity of God's exaltation is no light goal; human beings cannot undertake it through their own power, so seeking God's aid is necessary.
rows.anchor: abdin ‘acz-i zâtîsi kudret-i zâtiyesiyle böyle bir taahhüde girişmesine mâni‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isti‘ana means asking for aid or assistance; giving help is i‘ana, and mutual assistance is ta‘awun, so the terms must be distinguished.
rows.anchor: “İsti‘âne”, ‘avn talep etmek, ta‘bîr-i âhârla me‘ûnet istemek, daha Türkçesi yardım dilemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusive restriction here concerns asking for help; the omitted complement permits three readings: aid itself, aid in every matter, or aid in a specific matter.
rows.anchor: Bu isti‘ânenin ne gibi hususta olduğu zikr olunmamıştır. Böyle olan yerlerde de üç mâna muhtemel olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first and universal readings converge in meaning, though the first is more eloquent and the second more explicit.
rows.anchor: Bu ikisi meâlen birleşir. Fakat evvelki eblağ, bu sarih olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although worship could suggest a specific request for aid, the verse's monotheistic emphasis and context of God's exclusive praise require a general meaning.
rows.anchor: hepsi Allah’a mahsus olan hamdin beyânı siyâkında îrâd edilmiş bulunması

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's transmitted view supports the general scope of seeking aid, in worship and all other affairs.
rows.anchor: her hâlde İbn Abbas hazretlerinden de rivayet edildiği üzere umûmu muktezîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resulting meaning is that believers ask God alone for help both in worship and every other matter, unlike disbelievers who seek help elsewhere.
rows.anchor: Biz gerek sana ibadet ve itaatımızda ve gerek sâir umûrumuzun hepsinde ancak Senden isti‘âne ederiz

rows.speaker: Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Beydawi distinguishes necessary aid, without which an act cannot occur, from nonessential aid that makes it easier; necessary aid includes ability, conception, instruments, and material.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî’nin beyânına göre me‘ûnet iki nevidir. Birisine “me‘ûnet-i zarûriye”, diğerine “me‘ûnet-i gayr-i zarûriye” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal theory calls these two kinds of aid enabling power and facilitating power.
rows.anchor: Bu taksim ilm-i usûlde “kudret-i mümekkine” ve “kudret-i müyessire” nâmları tahtında yapılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All enabling aid belongs to God, but the request is ours; capability arises when human seeking and divine assistance coincide with the act, which is called acquisition or partial will.
rows.anchor: bütün me‘ûnet Allah’ındır, fakat talep bizimdir. Ve buna “kesb” veya “irâde-i cüz’iye” dahi tâbir olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are given authority to request; intended and unintended acts alike are attributed to us because they occur in and through us as their locus.
rows.anchor: bizden birisi talebimizle, diğeri talebimiz olmayarak iki fiil sâdır olur ve her ikisi de bizden sâdır olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In voluntary acts we are the proximate cause through our request, but not the complete cause, since we depend on necessary aid; the Creator makes the total causal set.
rows.anchor: Fakat bütün sebebi ve ‘illet-i tâmmesi biz değiliz, çünkü biz bunda me‘ûnet-i zarûriyeye muhtâcız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voluntary action expresses a relation between a requesting agent and a creating agent; bodies are inherently passive, while the soul is inherently desirous and God's action is creative.
rows.anchor: Demek ki ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyemiz bir fâ‘il-i tâlib ile bir fâ‘il-i hâlık arasındaki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The engine analogy distinguishes the machine as the locus of motion, the operator as the one who wants and initiates it, and God as the creator of the motion from nonexistence.
rows.anchor: İşleten, o hareketi isteyen makinisttir. Yaratan, o hareketi baştan nihâyete, ‘ademden vücûda getiren Hak teâlâ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account rejects both Jabriyya or materialist views that reduce people to soulless machines and the idea that humans create like God.
rows.anchor: ne Cebriyye veya Maddiyye gibi insanı rûhsuz bir makine farz ettirmeye çalışmalı, ne de onu rûh ve cismin hâlıkı olan Hak teâlâ gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Overindulging in metaphysical speculation until one loses the path and denies obvious truths leads to endless error.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-i zâhireyi inkâr eyleyecek bir surette dalıp gitmek sonu gelmeyen bir dalâlet olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request of existence is not existence itself: seeking is a relation among existents, not a created existent, so it entails neither infinite regress nor compulsion nor creation.
rows.anchor: Cebr lâzım gelmez, çünkü fiil araba sürükler gibi yapılmış değildir. Halk da lâzım gelmez, çünkü taleb bir mevcud değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universal will is created, while partial will, seeking, and choice called kasb are an uncreated relation belonging to us.
rows.anchor: irâde-i külliye denilen kuvve-i irâdiye mahluktur. Fakat irâde-i cüz’iye ve taleb ve ihtiyarla “kesb” dediğimiz karar gayr-i mahluktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The limits of understanding human willing reflect our inability to comprehend God's reality.
rows.anchor: taleb ve irâdenin hadd-i vücûdîsini, inniyyetini tamamen ihâta edemiyor isek o da Hak teâlâ’nın hakikatini muhît olmadığımızdan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse itself assigns the capacity to seek to us and assistance and power to God, excluding both Jabriyya compulsion and Qadariyya denial of destiny.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha’da نَسْتَعِينُ cümlesinin içinde taleb salâhiyeti bizim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is mistaken to infer that every partial will succeeds; when people fail, they may wrongly swing toward compulsion by treating willing as creation and assuming God cannot intervene.
rows.anchor: bunu yanlış anlıyorlar da bizim her irâde-i cüz’iyemizin her zaman iş görmekte kâfi olduğunu zannediyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can create outcomes that match or diverge from our seeking, grant extra favor to those on His path, or let others face loss, punishment, or reminders.
rows.anchor: o müvâzâtı ref‘ederek lehimize veya aleyhimize bizzat icrâ-yı tasarrufa ve ta‘bîr-i şer‘îsiyle nusret u hızlâna dahi kādir olduğunda şüphe edilemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about entrusting one's affair to God illustrates this subtlety concerning delegated trust.
rows.anchor: Dünyada dahi mükâfat ve mücâzat veya irâdesine ihtâr ve tenbih mânasını ifade eden bu noktalara müte‘allik birçok âyetler göreceğiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that when God wills to enact His decree, He removes the reason of people of understanding; this concerns good or bad seeking, not compulsion.
rows.anchor: “Allah teâlâ kazâ ve kaderini infâz etmek murad ederse zevi’l-‘ukūlün akıllarını alıverir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says people may dislike what is good for them and love what is harmful, since God knows while they do not.
rows.anchor: âyet-i celîlesi de bu nüktede diğer bir mâna ifade eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two declarative clauses also perform an implied act of commitment, like conventional oaths, covenants, or contracts; the prior speech signaled the obligation this acceptance entails.
rows.anchor: Görülüyor ki إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ iki kelâm-ı ihbârîden müteşekkil bir âyettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse records a profound covenant between God and servants, a mutual legal agreement that summarizes a fundamental practical and social law of nature.
rows.anchor: gayet derin ve gayet şümullü bir ‘akd-i bey‘at, bir mukāvele-i hukūkiye takrîr u tescîl edilmiş oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All living beings are carried by this covenantal law; disbelievers follow it unconsciously, while believers experience it consciously as well as bodily.
rows.anchor: ehl-i küfr bunun ardından lâ-şu‘ûrî olarak vücûden sürüklenir. Ehl-i iman da bunu vücûdundan başka vicdan ve şuuruyla dahi yaşar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the center of the Fatiha, speech and the covenant are voiced through the collective conscience and worshipful tongue, pointing to conscience as a locus for divine speech.
rows.anchor: Ne latîftir ki Fâtiha’nın tam ortasında hakk-ı tekellüm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links this point to the trustworthy Spirit bringing revelation to Muhammad's heart and to God's speaking to humans by revelation or from behind a veil.
rows.anchor: Bunda vicdân-ı ‘ubûdiyetin kelâm-ı ilâhîye tecellîgâh olduğuna büyük bir tenbih vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human speech and communication are gifts from the Creator, so people should hear, understand, and apply God's revealed eternal speech through their shared conscience.
rows.anchor: söylemek, teblîğ-i merâm etmek kudret ve sıfatını Hâlıkınızdan ve O’nun me‘ûnetinden ahz ediyorsunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God models gracious reciprocal dealing: after creating and nurturing people, He gives worldly gifts as if their property and makes them eternal, granting them a nearly equal standing in the agreement.
rows.anchor: dünyada muvakkaten ihsan buyurduğu ‘atâyâsını bizim milk-i hakīkīmiz imiş gibi ebedîleştirmek ve ebediyyen tenmiye etmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although humans have no inherent rights before God, He recognizes their rights and assumes them under His mercy; worship is His right and the servant's duty, while aid, reward, and punishment become human claims by His own commitment.
rows.anchor: zâtında hiçbir hukūku olmayan bizlere dahi milk ve hukūk tanıyarak ikisini mübâdele ediyor ve bizim hukūkumuzu da ‘uhde-i rahmetine alıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rights of people receive even greater care than God's rights; mercy precedes worship, worship precedes asking for help, and duty precedes the claim to a right, though divine mercy establishes the right first.
rows.anchor: Rahmet ubûdiyete mütekaddim, lâkin ubûdiyet de isti‘âneye mütekaddim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects this reciprocal moral pattern to the Prophetic hadith, 'Adopt the character traits of God.'
rows.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfinde işaret buyurduğu ahlâk-ı ilâhiyenin en şâyân-ı hayret tecellîlerinden biridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'we worship / we ask help' gives social community special importance, since the pledge is not expressed in the singular.
rows.anchor: akid “ibadet ederim, isti‘âne ederim” gibi mütekellim vahde, yani ferd sîgasıyla yapılmıyor da, نَعْبُدُ / نَسْتَعِينُ diye cemi‘yani

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: Exegetes see an indication here of the virtue of congregational worship.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn burada cemaatle ibadetin faziletine işaret vardır diyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A congregation is not a mere crowd but an organized body able to act with one spirit, formed through a shared social covenant, so there is no true circularity in the verse.
rows.anchor: cemaat kuru bir kalabalık demek değil, rûh-i vâhidle hareket edebilen bir hey’et-i muntazama-i vahdâniye demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Social spirit first takes root in individuals when fraternity widens conscience beyond pride, narrowness, and selfishness; this breadth can support anything from a family to an empire.
rows.anchor: Rûh-i ictimâ‘î evvelâ ferdde teessüs eder, vicdân-ı ferde ne vakit hiss-i uhuvvet girer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Narrowness of conscience accompanies ignorance and pride, while an expanded conscience accompanies elevated understanding, humility, mercy, patience, and forbearance; the narrow-hearted person loves and fears only himself.
rows.anchor: Vicdan darlığı cehalet ve kibir ile mütelâzımdır. İnşirâh-ı sadr dahi denilen vicdan vüs‘ati ise hafv u recâda
